title: Shielded-Connection liveness probe: after every PRL handshake, send host-TRNG data through the tunnel to a command whose response is a deterministic function of that data (CalcHash) and compare locally — a replayed session cannot answer
threat: Whole-session replay of a captured OPTIGA unlock session (OP17-2): the Infineon PRL handshake carries only the chip's random_S, so an interposer that recorded one genuine session can replay the chip's frames to the MCU; the vendor-faithful ProVerif model proves inj-agreement false. Combined with a substituted/absent chip this lets a bus device impersonate the OPTIGA for the duration of a session.
proposal: In `OptigaTrustM::ensure_shield`, immediately after `establish()` succeeds, draw 32 B from `rng_strong`, send OPTIGA `CalcHash(SHA-256, data)` (cmd 0x30, non-counter-bound, no AC) inside the shield, and compare the returned digest against a locally computed SHA-256 (HW HASH) with FI-double sentinel checks; mismatch → `ShieldError::Replay`, tear down, hard-reset, D1-inconclusive classification (no page-124 charge). Because the replayed transcript's CalcHash response was computed over the old data, the compare fails with certainty; the probe costs one APDU (~5 ms). Document the residual honestly: this closes session-level replay by a bus adversary but not an adversary holding the PBS (who can run a real handshake).
rationale: Trezor has the identical gap (optiga_transport.c:771-780, no master random) and has not closed it; this is a one-APDU 'beyond' fix that needs no change to the chip's protocol, keeps every existing sequence-counter/nonce-wrap guard, and makes #117 falsifiable on the bench (record a session with the LA1010, replay it, assert the probe refuses). It also upgrades the `random()` path: a replayed session would otherwise return recorded TRNG bytes into the 3-source XOR.
repo_evidence: secure/src/optiga/shield.rs:698-700 comment: 'Infineon PRL does NOT send a master random — the handshake uses only random_S from SlaveHello'
secure/src/optiga/shield.rs — grep 'freshness|liveness' hits only sequence-counter comments (:169,:646,:885); no post-handshake challenge
secure/src/optiga/mod.rs:532-600 ensure_shield: establish → active, no probe
contracts/verification/docs/THREAT_CLAIM_MAP.md:73 — vendor-faithful model proves replay possible; Issue #117 (OP17-2) OPEN; #396
vendor_precedent: none (Trezor core/embed/sec/optiga/optiga_transport.c:747-838 has the same handshake without a host nonce); analogous host-chosen-challenge pattern in Trezor's AUTOREF set_auto_state over an SE nonce (optiga_commands.c:561-619), inverted here.
risks: CalcHash availability/AC at the production LcsO must be confirmed on the V3 part (it is a standard Trust M command); the probe must run before any counter-bound command so a replay cannot burn E120; a transport failure in the probe must be inconclusive, not 'replay detected' (otherwise an interposer gains a lock/DoS lever); update the ProVerif model (optiga_shield_handshake_vendor.pv) with the probe to turn the do-not-cite row into a cited claim.
